title: if, else if, else
learningObjectives: Explain if, else if, else and choose an appropriate control-flow structure.

understand.concept: The if statement executes a block when its condition is truthy. else provides an alternative block, and else if checks additional conditions in sequence. Conditions are converted to booleans using JavaScript truthiness.
understand.whyItMatters: Branching lets a program choose actions based on data and user state. Keep conditions readable and order them from the most specific cases to broader fallbacks.
understand.analogy: A conditional is a decision point with paths that depend on the result of a question.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript control flow follows precise condition evaluation and iteration semantics.

explain.narrative: The score is below 80 but at least 50, so the second branch runs and prints Passed.

examples.explanation: The score is below 80 but at least 50, so the second branch runs and prints Passed.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the sequence or branch results described.

practise.guidedTask: Write a grading program with three ranges. Test boundary values just below, at, and above each threshold.
practise.independentTask: Write a small program that uses the control-flow structure to process learner or course data. Test normal, boundary, and empty cases.
hints: Use strict comparisons for exact values.
Choose for...of for iterable values and avoid confusing keys with values.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>if, else if, else</title></head><body>
<script>const score=72;if(score>=80){console.log('Excellent');}else if(score>=50){console.log('Passed');}else{console.log('Try again');}</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which block runs when no if or else if condition is true and an else block exists?
questions.explanation: The else block runs when none of the preceding conditions is truthy.

questions.prompt: What should you verify when writing a loop?
options: That its condition and updates allow it to terminate as intended
questions.answer: That its condition and updates allow it to terminate as intended
questions.explanation: Correct termination and boundary handling prevent infinite loops and skipped work.
